newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products--Conventional gasoline diffs ease.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products--Conventional gasoline diffs ease.

text.p: Conventional gasoline differentials in New York Harbor, the Gulf Coast and the Midcontinent fell back Friday, partially offsetting the gains made on the NYMEX.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline was up 0.52 cent at 57.60 cents a gallon and July heating oil gained 0.38 cent at 52.00 cents a gallon.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline differentials weakened early in the day, with traders reporting several deals done at 2.60 cents under the July NYMEX, down about 0.20 cent from Thursday levels.
Ample supplies, despite the closed arbitrage window with Europe, have kept gasoline differentials under pressure, according to market players.
Distillate trading appeared sluggish, with few barrels changing hands.
"Sun Co has been leading the market lower this week with weak offers, but they don't have anything to sell," one traders said.
Prompt heating oil was offered at 0.25 cent under the July NYMEX, and prompt low sulphur diesel was offered at 0.60 cent--though traders said it would be difficult to move barrels at those levels.
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials continued to erode Friday, with offers sliding back to 2.70 cents under the July NYMEX price for a dip of 0.45 cent from late Thursday, traders said.
That drop extended the one cent decline in the M1 differentials seen Thursday.
However, premium grade conventional V1 gasoline held its healthy 5.25 cent-premium to the M1 grade, traders said, aided by concerns about possible refinery problems in the region.
Prompt premium reformulated D1 gasoline was talked near 4.75 cents over the July NYMEX, also holding part of its recent strength, traders said.

Midcontinent markets were softer to unchanged in quiet trade on Friday. Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials lost some of its strength from earlier in the week, dropping a half cent amid light selling. Deals were heard done between 5.60/5.75 cents over the July NYMEX print although nothing was confirmed.
Chicago unleaded differentials also came down about 0.20 cent to 4.00/4.30 cents.
Some traders said they expected differentials to firm again, citing a handful of shorts for the 17th Explorer cycle. The 17th cycle has been delayed nine days until July 1st or 2nd.
